newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Israeli settlements a time bomb.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Israeli settlements a time bomb.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in remarks published on Sunday that Israeli settlement expansion in occupied Arab lands was a time bomb waiting to explode.

"Instead of implementing what the agreements demand, they decide to expand settlements. (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu knows that's a time bomb with many risks," the Israeli Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper quoted Arafat as saying.

Netanyahu said on Sunday there was "clear information" that Palestinians were planning to launch another wave of violence similar to the one in September when 15 Israelis and 60 Palestinians were killed in gun battles throughout the West Banka and Gaza.
"Talk of us igniting the territories is cheap propoganda which belies unclean intentions," Arafat told the newspaper in an interview.

Netanyahu's government, formed six months ago, has approved construction of thousands of new housing units in settlements in the West Bank and Gaza where 140,000 Jews have settled among two million Palestinians.

His cabinet decided on Friday to reinstate financial benefits to settlements in the West Bank after a guerrilla attack in which a settler and her son were killed. Israel's former government, which concluded peace interim deals with the Palestinians, had cancelled the benefits.
